ORG-01.prompt: You are starting a larger project. How likely are you to first work out the next concrete steps before you get going?

EXP-01.prompt: Someone suggests a new approach to your team. You immediately feel: "I know this, I have been through something like it before," but you cannot explain why just yet. How strongly does this first impression influence your assessment?

VOICE-01.prompt: Your team has already more or less agreed on a decision. You notice another point against it. How likely are you to raise it anyway?

AMB-01.prompt: You receive different feedback on a new idea and cannot yet tell which feedback is more relevant. How uncomfortable does this feel?

EL-01.prompt: You are choosing between two approaches, both of which you could try on a small scale. How likely are you to test something before deciding?

EVI-01.prompt: You have three options, and one immediately appeals to you most. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: Before committing, I deliberately look for counterarguments so I can spot weaknesses early.
alternatives.B: I start with my favorite to make progress and watch along the way for solid reasons against it.

EXP-02.prompt: A plan looks coherent on paper, but your experience from earlier situations makes you hesitate. How strongly does this prior experience influence your judgment of the plan?

ORG-03.prompt: Several important tasks compete for your attention at the same time. Which describes the way you work better?

alternatives.A: I keep several topics moving in parallel so that nothing comes to a complete stop.
alternatives.B: I focus on a few things and accept that others must wait.

AMB-02.prompt: A problem comes up and there are several plausible explanations, but for now there is no way to find out which one is actually right. How uncomfortable does this uncertainty feel?

VOICE-02.prompt: You learn something that matters to your work together but could weigh on the mood in the team. How likely are you to bring it up soon?

EVI-02.prompt: Your next step hinges on an assumption you are not yet sure about. How likely are you to deliberately check it before you commit?

EXP-03.prompt: Two options look equally good on the facts alone. But one of them strongly reminds you of earlier situations. How strongly does this personal experience tip your choice?

AMB-04.prompt: You are analyzing a problem, but every new piece of information makes the overall picture more confusing and raises further questions. How uncomfortable does this feel?

ORG-04.prompt: A task takes much longer than expected. Which describes the way you work better?

alternatives.A: I finish the task I started as planned before I rearrange the schedule.
alternatives.B: I adjust my schedule to the delay early, before I continue.

EL-02.prompt: Your team has two plausible approaches and the discussion is not moving forward. Both could be tried with little effort. How likely are you to suggest a concrete test?

EXP-04.prompt: You face a challenge you have encountered several times in a similar form. How strongly do you draw on those experiences to assess what matters this time?

VOICE-03.prompt: A difficult topic was postponed and never revisited. Something important remains unresolved for you. How likely are you to put the topic back on the table yourself?

EL-05.prompt: An initial attempt gives no clear answer. How likely are you to deliberately change one thing and try again?

AMB-05.prompt: You need to keep working on something even though an important question remains open. How uncomfortable does this feel?

ORG-02.prompt: A task runs over several weeks, and nobody sets interim deadlines for you. How likely are you to set your own milestones to check where you stand?

EVI-03.prompt: You have made a decision. Shortly afterward, new information comes up that argues against it. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I reopen the decision right away and check whether I should change course.
alternatives.B: I stick with the decision for now and check whether the new information carries enough weight to change course.

EL-04.prompt: You are unsure how the market will respond to a new feature or offer. How likely are you to show potential users a simple first version early (for example, a sketch or a mock-up) instead of finishing it internally?

VOICE-04.prompt: A decision is made that you consider wrong from a professional perspective. How likely are you to tell your team that you see the situation differently?

EVI-05.prompt: Someone on the team sees something differently and raises a point that makes sense. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I go through the point right away and question my own assessment.
alternatives.B: I stick with my assessment for now and look for further evidence that supports or weakens the point.

EXP-06.prompt: You need to make a decision even though some information is still missing. But you know the field very well. How strongly do you rely on your own experience when you choose?

VOICE-05.prompt: The group wants to close a topic, but an important point remains open for you. How likely are you to say that you are not ready yet?

ORG-07.prompt: You are concentrating on an important topic when another important request comes in. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I interrupt my work fairly quickly and take care of the new request right away.
alternatives.B: I first stay with what I am working on and push the new request back.

EVI-06.prompt: Two sources you generally consider reliable contradict each other on an important question. How likely are you to look more closely at why they differ?

ORG-08.prompt: Your plan still basically works, but several smaller things turn out differently than expected. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I only change my plan when the deviations really start to carry weight.
alternatives.B: I prefer to keep adjusting my plan even for smaller changes.
